hero.headline: Key US surveillance authority set to expire as Congress remains deadlocked
hero.body:
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act is on track to lapse Friday after Congress failed to reach agreement on renewing the spy tool. The authority allows US intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets outside the United States without a warrant and has been credited with providing more than half the content in the president's daily briefing.

Lawmakers in both parties have warned that allowing Section 702 to expire could threaten national security operations. Intelligence officials say the authority has helped prevent terror plots and other security threats. If the law lapses, intelligence agencies and telecommunications companies face legal uncertainty about ongoing surveillance activities.

The appointment of Bill Pulte as director of national intelligence has complicated renewal talks. Pulte lacks national security experience and has drawn criticism from lawmakers in both parties as a Trump loyalist. His selection has created new friction in negotiations that were already stalled over privacy concerns and oversight provisions.

The dispute over Section 702 reflects broader tensions over government surveillance powers and civil liberties protections. Privacy advocates have long pushed for reforms to prevent warrantless searches of Americans' communications that are incidentally collected under the program. Those reform efforts have clashed with intelligence officials who argue the tool is essential for tracking foreign threats.

Beyond the immediate Section 702 debate, civil liberties groups are raising concerns about how the government plans to use artificial intelligence for domestic surveillance. According to recent reporting, the Pentagon has sought to deploy AI tools to analyze bulk commercial data about Americans, including geolocation and web browsing information. Privacy advocates argue that AI could dramatically expand surveillance capabilities by automating the analysis of vast datasets at scale.

The concern centers on how federal agencies already purchase Americans' private data from commercial sources without court approval. Immigration enforcement agencies have used purchased cellphone location data and license plate information to target communities. The addition of AI tools could make this data collection and analysis faster, cheaper, and more comprehensive.

Civil liberties organizations warn that without new congressional safeguards, the combination of bulk data collection and AI analysis could lead to mass domestic surveillance. They point to historical examples of government surveillance abuses and argue that current laws have not kept pace with technological capabilities. The concern is that AI tools could enable the government to build detailed profiles of individuals' movements, associations, and political views with minimal human oversight.

Congress has until Friday to pass legislation extending Section 702 or face the first-ever lapse of the authority since its creation. The approaching deadline has not yet forced a breakthrough in negotiations between the White House and Capitol Hill. The broader questions about AI-powered surveillance and civil liberties protections remain unresolved.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran Exchange Strikes for Second Day, Threatening Cease-Fire
cards.teaser: The United States and Iran traded military strikes across the Middle East for a second consecutive day, raising fears of a return to broader conflict.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran traded military strikes across the Middle East for a second consecutive day. Iran responded to U.S. attacks by targeting American assets in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain, with Bahrain reporting damage to its capital overnight. Tehran said the latest U.S. strikes rendered the existing cease-fire meaningless.

The escalating exchanges have raised concerns about a return to all-out war after a period of relative calm. Negotiations to end the conflict remain stalled, with Iran insisting it will maintain control of the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump warned that Tehran would pay the price for rejecting a proposed deal as both sides demonstrate willingness to continue military engagement.

cards.headline: Oil prices jump as US-Iran conflict escalates into second day
cards.body:
Oil prices rose after the United States and Iran exchanged fire for a second consecutive day, raising concerns that the two nations could return to open military conflict. The price increase reflected market anxiety over potential disruptions to global energy supplies as tensions in the Middle East intensified.

The renewed hostilities mark a significant escalation in relations between Washington and Tehran. The United States launched a new round of attacks against Iranian targets, prompting a military response from Iran. The exchanges followed an initial confrontation between the two countries the previous day.

Energy markets responded quickly to the developments, with traders factoring in the risk of supply disruptions from the oil-rich region. The Middle East remains a critical source of global petroleum supplies, and any sustained conflict in the area has the potential to affect international energy prices and availability. Market participants are monitoring the situation closely for signs of further escalation or diplomatic resolution.

The conflict has created uncertainty for global energy markets at a time when prices were already under pressure from various economic factors. European markets are particularly sensitive to Middle East instability, as the region supplies a significant portion of energy imports to European nations. The European Central Bank has indicated it plans to raise interest rates in response to inflation driven partly by energy disruptions related to the Iran situation.

The military exchanges between the United States and Iran represent the most serious direct confrontation between the two countries in recent years. The duration and intensity of the conflict will determine its ultimate impact on global oil markets and broader economic conditions. Investors and policymakers are watching to see whether diplomatic channels can de-escalate the situation or whether the military engagement will continue.

cards.headline: US inflation reaches fastest pace in three years
cards.teaser: President Trump commented on rising consumer prices, later clarifying his remarks about inflation levels.
cards.body:
Consumer prices in the United States have risen at their fastest rate in three years. President Trump initially said he loved the inflation rate, but later clarified that he meant he was pleased inflation had not climbed even higher.

The sharp increase in prices marks a significant acceleration that affects American household budgets across goods and services. The Federal Reserve is considering monetary policy decisions to balance price stability with economic growth.

cards.headline: Trump pushes third reconciliation bill with $350 billion for Defense Department
cards.teaser: The president called on Congress to immediately pass legislation that includes the Save America Act.
cards.body:
President Trump called on Republicans to immediately pass a third reconciliation bill worth $350 billion on Wednesday. The legislation would direct substantial funding to the Department of Defense and include the Save America Act, which Trump requested be added to the package.

The push represents Trump's effort to accelerate work on the spending measure, which is still being developed on Capitol Hill. The president framed the Defense Department funding as a key element of his legislative priorities as Republicans work to shape their next spending bill.

cards.headline: Trump intelligence nominee raises concerns over surveillance program renewal
cards.teaser: Bill Pulte's appointment has disrupted congressional negotiations to renew FISA 702, a key surveillance tool used by U.S. intelligence agencies.
cards.body:
President Trump is moving forward with his plan to appoint Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence. Trump stated that Pulte has been tasked with executing a "downsizing" of the intelligence director's office.

The appointment has drawn intense criticism from lawmakers concerned about Pulte's qualifications for the role. Congress is under pressure to pass a short-term extension of a surveillance law set to expire, with the debate now complicated by concerns over Pulte's suitability to oversee the nation's intelligence operations.

cards.headline: SpaceX files for IPO seeking to raise $75 billion
cards.body:
SpaceX has confidentially filed for an initial public offering on the US stock market, according to Bloomberg and the Wall Street Journal. The filing represents one of the most closely watched listings in market history, with the rocket company potentially seeking a valuation exceeding $1.75 trillion.

The confidential filing gives regulators time to review SpaceX's financial disclosures before the information becomes public. An IPO could occur as early as June, marking what is expected to be a major year for large-scale public offerings.

SpaceX, founded by Elon Musk, has become a dominant force in space travel and satellite communications. The company operates through several divisions, including its Starlink subsidiary, which has grown into one of the world's largest satellite operators. Starlink's satellite internet service generates over half of SpaceX's revenue and has become influential in geopolitical operations, with users ranging from NASA to foreign militaries.

The company holds extensive contracts with the US government for defense and space operations. NASA depends heavily on SpaceX rockets for the majority of its launches, making the space program substantially reliant on Musk's enterprise.

In February, SpaceX acquired Musk's artificial intelligence company xAI, which owns the social media platform X and produces the Grok chatbot. The acquisition valued xAI at $250 billion. SpaceX cited plans to build solar-powered datacenters in space to support AI infrastructure and meet growing computational demands. However, xAI has lagged behind competitors like Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT in capability development.

SpaceX's strategic focus has recently shifted toward orbital datacenters and supporting NASA's upcoming moon landing missions. Mars colonization, long a prominent Musk objective, has become less emphasized in recent communications.

The $75 billion fundraising target would rank among the largest IPOs in American history. Two additional AI companies are expected to follow with major public offerings this year. OpenAI announced a $122 billion funding round and plans its own IPO, while fellow AI firm Anthropic is preparing a similar public debut. SpaceX's performance as the first of these three offerings could shape investor reception for subsequent listings.

Details of SpaceX's finances have remained closely guarded even from most investors. Share pricing and other listing specifics will become public following SEC review of the confidential filing. SpaceX is working with prominent international banks, including Barclays, to coordinate the IPO process.

For Musk, already the world's richest person, a successful offering would significantly expand his wealth and position him closer to becoming the world's first trillionaire.

hero.headline: South Korea Fines E-Commerce Giant Coupang Record $409 Million
hero.teaser: The penalty against the U.S.-incorporated company has created diplomatic tension between Seoul and Washington.
hero.body:
South Korea's Coupang Fine Sparks Diplomatic Tensions With Washington

South Korean regulators imposed a record $409 million fine on Coupang, an e-commerce company incorporated in the United States but operating primarily in South Korea. The penalty follows a regulatory investigation into the company's business practices, but the case has escalated into a significant diplomatic dispute between Seoul and Washington.

Coupang, often called South Korea's answer to Amazon, is headquartered in Seattle and listed on the New York Stock Exchange. The company is run by Korean-American billionaire Bom Kim. The regulatory action stems from a data breach that occurred in November when a former employee stole an internal security key, compromising data from 33.7 million users.

South Korea's response to the breach has been forceful. Police raided the company's Seoul headquarters, tax authorities launched a special audit, and parliament summoned executives for questioning. Bom Kim refused to travel to Korea for hearings, citing his role as a global chief executive. Korean police subsequently requested that immigration authorities notify them if he enters the country.

According to South Korean broadcaster SBS, Washington signaled it would not proceed with high-level diplomatic and defence consultations unless South Korea guaranteed Kim would face no legal consequences related to the data breach. South Korea's foreign ministry has not denied the report but stated that security discussions should proceed separately from the Coupang matter and that investigations would continue under Korean law.

The dispute has affected broader negotiations between the two countries. SBS reported that the tensions have influenced talks on US support for South Korea's development of nuclear-powered submarines, with a scheduled visit from a US delegation reportedly postponed.

The Coupang issue represents one of several tensions between Seoul and Washington under the Trump administration. In September, an immigration raid at a Hyundai-LG battery plant in Georgia detained more than 300 South Korean workers. The US has also restricted intelligence sharing after South Korea's unification minister publicly identified a suspected North Korean nuclear site. In January, Trump threatened to raise tariffs on South Korean goods from 15 percent to 25 percent.

Coupang has significantly increased its lobbying efforts in Washington. The company spent over $3 million lobbying the US government in 2025 and doubled its spending in the first quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. In April, 54 Republican members of Congress wrote to South Korea's ambassador accusing Seoul of "discriminatory actions" against US companies.

Five US investment firms holding Coupang shares have filed notices of intent to pursue arbitration against South Korea under the US-Korea free trade agreement, claiming Seoul's enforcement response was disproportionate. The arbitration process remains active.

Experts suggest the dispute reflects how the Trump administration increasingly links economic and security issues, potentially affecting cooperation on nuclear agreements and technology sharing.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran Exchange Strikes for Second Day, Threatening Cease-Fire
cards.teaser: The United States and Iran traded military strikes across the Middle East for a second consecutive day, raising fears of a return to broader conflict.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran traded military strikes across the Middle East for a second consecutive day. Iran responded to U.S. attacks by targeting American assets in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain, with Bahrain reporting damage to its capital overnight. cards.headline: Women Who Fled Iran Face Deportation to Central African Republic
cards.teaser: Lawyers say nearly two dozen people are slated for removal to a country the U.S. advises against traveling to for any reason.
cards.body:
A group of women who fled Iran are set to be deported to the Central African Republic, according to lawyers representing them. The women are among nearly two dozen people scheduled for removal to the country.

The U.S. State Department has issued a Level 4 travel advisory for the Central African Republic, its highest warning level, advising Americans to not travel there for any reason. The lawyers have raised concerns about the safety of deporting the women to such a destination.

cards.headline: Protests Planned at Mexico City Stadium Ahead of World Cup Opening
cards.teaser: Unions and other groups intend to demonstrate at the capital's World Cup venue as the tournament begins.
cards.body:
Labor unions and advocacy groups plan to demonstrate at Mexico City's Azteca Stadium during the World Cup opening ceremony. This marks the third time Mexico City is hosting World Cup matches, and protesters intend to use the high-profile platform to draw attention to their causes.

The stadium has undergone renovations ahead of the tournament's start. Organizers have not announced adjustments to security or ceremony plans in response to the planned demonstrations.

cards.headline: Mexico's President to Skip World Cup Opening, Breaking Tradition
cards.teaser: Claudia Sheinbaum plans to intentionally avoid the entire tournament, ending decades of sports diplomacy.
cards.body:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum will not attend the World Cup opening match or any games during the tournament, marking a significant break from decades of tradition. Mexican presidents have historically participated in major sporting events as part of sports diplomacy, using these occasions to demonstrate national unity and pride.

The decision comes as protests threaten to disrupt Mexico City's World Cup opening ceremony, with unions and other groups planning demonstrations at the stadium. This adds another layer of tension to the much-watched event.

cards.headline: Trump-Endorsed Candidate in Colombia Sparks Debate on Masculinity
cards.teaser: Women's rights groups say the presidential front-runner is deploying a familiar right-wing playbook.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential front-runner, who has received an endorsement from former U.S. President Trump, has ignited a national conversation about masculinity and machismo. The candidate's rhetoric and campaign style have drawn scrutiny from women's rights organizations.

Activists say they recognize the candidate's approach as part of a broader far-right political strategy seen in other countries. The debate has become a central theme in Colombia's presidential race as voters prepare to cast ballots.

cards.headline: French Singer Patrick Bruel Under Formal Investigation for Rape
cards.teaser: The entertainer was released from custody under judicial supervision while a magistrate investigates.
cards.body:
French singer Patrick Bruel has been placed under formal investigation for rape and sexual assault. The 67-year-old was released from custody and placed under judicial supervision while an examining magistrate conducts a deeper investigation.

Bruel has been charged in connection with four cases involving allegations of rape, attempted rape, sexual assault, and sexual harassment. He has denied all charges. The case represents one of the most significant MeToo allegations in the French music industry, with more than 20 women making allegations against the singer and actor dating back to the 1990s.

cards.headline: Queens neighborhoods celebrate as World Cup begins
cards.teaser: Residents along the 7 train corridor in Queens are embracing the World Cup, reflecting the borough's diverse immigrant communities for whom soccer holds deep cultural significance.
cards.body:
The 2026 World Cup is being played in New Jersey, but in Queens, New York, the tournament holds deep significance for the borough's immigrant communities. Along the 7 train route, residents from around the world are embracing soccer as more than just a sport—it's a central part of their culture and way of life.

For these diverse neighborhoods, the World Cup provides a connection to their countries of origin and creates shared experiences across Queens' multicultural communities.

cards.headline: Scientists release winning images from research photo contest
cards.teaser: Five photographs showcasing scientific work, from neon mosquitoes to bird migrations, have been selected as winners of a contest highlighting research and discovery.
cards.body:
A photo competition has recognized five winning images that showcase scientific research and discovery across multiple disciplines. The photographs capture moments from various fields of study and include striking images such as fluorescent mosquitoes and migratory birds in flight.

The contest highlights the visual and aesthetic dimensions of scientific work alongside its technical aspects. These selected images demonstrate how photography can reveal both the wonder and the practical realities of conducting research in the natural world.

cards.headline: World Cup tournament expands to record 48 teams and 1,248 players
cards.teaser: The 2026 FIFA World Cup features the largest field in tournament history, with 48 national teams and 1,248 players competing.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup will feature a record 48 teams and 1,248 players across all squads, marking a significant expansion from the traditional 32-team format. This larger tournament structure opens participation to more nations than ever before.

The expanded competition has generated considerable statistics and facts about the event. With teams and players from across the globe converging for the tournament, there is no shortage of notable figures and records surrounding the 2026 World Cup.

cards.headline: Medieval mathematician gave his name to modern algorithms
cards.teaser: The term algorithm derives from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Kharizmi, a 9th-century Persian mathematician who advanced algebra and promoted the use of zero.
cards.body:
In the 9th century, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Kharizmi made lasting contributions to mathematics by helping solidify the concept of algorithms. He popularized algebraic methods and championed the use of zero in mathematical notation, innovations that would shape the discipline for centuries to come.

His influence extends into the modern era through the word "algorithm" itself, which derives from his name. Today, algorithms are fundamental to computer science and digital technology, applied billions of times daily across computing and data processing.

cards.headline: Azteca Stadium reopens after renovations ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Mexico's Azteca Stadium has completed renovations and reopened in time to host matches in the 2026 World Cup tournament.
cards.body:
Mexico's Estadio Azteca, officially renamed Estadio Ciudad de México for the tournament, has completed renovations ahead of the 2026 World Cup. The iconic venue, considered the western hemisphere's cathedral of football, will host the opening match on Thursday when Mexico plays South Africa.

Media were granted access to tour the renovated facility before the tournament begins. The stadium, one of the world's most recognizable soccer venues, will once again serve as a key international competition venue.

cards.headline: European Central Bank to raise interest rates as inflation rises
cards.teaser: The bank plans its first rate increase since September 2023 as energy disruptions from the Iran conflict drive higher prices across the continent.
cards.body:
The European Central Bank is set to raise interest rates for the first time since September 2023, as inflation pressures mount across the continent. The rate increase comes amid energy disruptions stemming from the conflict between the United States and Iran, which have driven prices higher throughout Europe.

Europe's heavy dependence on Middle Eastern energy imports makes the region particularly vulnerable to supply shocks from the area. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has significantly affected energy prices, contributing to inflation that the ECB aims to combat through its rate increase to maintain price stability.

cards.headline: US inflation reaches fastest pace in three years
cards.teaser: President Trump commented on rising consumer prices, later clarifying his remarks about inflation levels.
cards.body:
Consumer prices in the United States have risen at their fastest rate in three years. President Trump initially said he loved the inflation rate, but later clarified that he meant he was pleased inflation had not climbed even higher.

The sharp increase in prices marks a significant acceleration that affects American household budgets across goods and services. The Federal Reserve is considering monetary policy decisions to balance price stability with economic growth.

cards.headline: South Korea fines e-commerce company record $400 million over data breach
cards.teaser: The penalty follows a breach that exposed the private data of approximately 37.5 million users.
cards.body:
South Korean regulators imposed a $400 million fine on a major e-commerce company following a data breach that exposed private information for approximately 37.5 million users. The penalty is the largest fine ever issued for a data breach in South Korea's history.

The enforcement action reflects intensifying regulatory scrutiny over data security practices in the digital commerce sector. The company, often compared to Amazon, now faces increased pressure to strengthen its safeguards for customer information.

cards.headline: Oracle reports earnings as cloud business undergoes rapid transformation
cards.teaser: The company beat earnings expectations but faced investor concerns over plans to raise an additional $20 billion amid heavy AI infrastructure spending.
cards.body:
Oracle reported quarterly earnings that exceeded analyst expectations for revenue, though the company's stock price declined following the announcement. The software company disclosed plans to raise another $20 billion to fund ongoing investments in cloud infrastructure and artificial intelligence capabilities.

Oracle's spending on AI infrastructure surpassed estimates, raising concerns among investors about the company's growing debt levels. The cloud business showed strong growth as Oracle continues transitioning from its traditional database software roots to cloud-based services. The company's data center build-out requires substantial capital investment as it competes with larger cloud providers in the rapidly expanding AI market.

cards.headline: Stock markets fall as investors weigh inflation and Iran conflict
cards.teaser: US stock futures fluctuated while major indexes declined more than one percent on concerns over rising prices and military tensions.
cards.body:
US stock markets declined as investors reacted to inflation reaching 4.2% in May, the highest rate in three years, alongside escalating military tensions between the United States and Iran. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 950 points, while the S&P 500 fell 1.6 percent and the Nasdaq tumbled 2 percent.

Inflation has risen for three consecutive months since the Iran conflict began, driven partly by energy price increases following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The US and Iran exchanged strikes for a second day, with Iran targeting American assets in Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain, intensifying concerns about further economic disruption.

cards.headline: Chinese companies dominate global robot parts manufacturing
cards.teaser: China's electric vehicle industry has enabled robotics manufacturers to produce components at unprecedented scale and low cost.
cards.body:
Chinese companies have established dominance in the global market for robot parts, building on the country's extensive electric vehicle industry infrastructure. Manufacturers in China produce robotic components at a scale and price point that competitors in other countries cannot match.

The robotics supply chain leverages China's existing capabilities in battery technology, motors, and precision manufacturing developed for electric vehicles. This industrial base allows Chinese firms to offer robot parts at prices significantly below those of manufacturers in other regions. Companies attempting to build robots outside China face significant cost and supply challenges due to the concentration of component production.

hero.headline: Apple unveils new Siri with advanced AI capabilities
hero.body:
Apple announced a major overhaul of Siri at its annual developer conference, introducing a redesigned voice assistant powered by generative artificial intelligence. The updated system, called "Siri AI," will integrate with Apple's broader artificial intelligence initiative known as Apple Intelligence and represents a significant shift in how the company approaches voice assistance.

The new Siri will operate differently from its predecessor, functioning more like AI chatbots such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini rather than a simple question-and-answer tool. Mike Rockwell, Apple's vice-president of Siri engineering, explained that the company rebuilt the tool with generative AI at its core. The assistant will feature its own dedicated app and offer a more conversational interface that can access Apple's native applications across mobile devices and laptops.

During a demonstration, Rockwell showed how the updated Siri can handle complex tasks. He asked it to identify a beach location from a photograph, then requested a friend's address nearby, and finally obtained directions to Santa Cruz with a stop at his friend's house, all within the Siri interface rather than jumping between multiple applications. The tool will also be able to proofread documents, assist with shopping, add calendar events, and retrieve information from images, such as nutritional data from photographs of food.

The partnership powering Siri AI's capabilities involves a billion-dollar agreement with Google. Siri's revamp relies on Google's Gemini AI model, marking a significant collaboration between the two technology companies. Initially, the new Siri will only be available in English, with a wider release scheduled for fall.

The overhaul comes after years of criticism that Apple's AI efforts lagged behind competitors like Google. Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice-president of software engineering, acknowledged the disparity during the conference, stating that some companies appear to be "racing forward, seemingly pursuing AI for the sake of AI, without clear regard for the people that it's ultimately meant to serve."

Apple has a history of delays with Siri updates. The company first announced an updated version in 2024 but postponed its release. Previous announcements about the assistant's capabilities also led to legal challenges. In May, Apple agreed to pay 250 million dollars to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging that the company falsely advertised Siri's artificial intelligence capabilities. Some consumers received settlements of up to 95 dollars.

Beyond Siri, Apple introduced additional AI features integrated into Safari, text messaging, and its Home app. The company also announced new camera and photo tools that use artificial intelligence to create, alter, or enhance images, all developed in collaboration with Google.

cards.headline: Former xAI engineer sues over alleged firing for safety concerns
cards.teaser: A former xAI employee filed a lawsuit claiming termination for raising AI safety issues about Grok.
cards.body:
A former xAI engineer has filed a lawsuit against the company and SpaceX, claiming he was fired for raising safety concerns about Grok, the AI system developed by xAI. According to the legal filing, the termination occurred shortly before SpaceX's initial public offering.

The engineer alleges the dismissal was retaliation for voicing his concerns about Grok's safety internally within the company.

cards.headline: Microsoft CEO pushes back on excessive AI token usage
cards.teaser: Satya Nadella addressed concerns about AI overuse at Microsoft in recent interviews.
cards.body:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella discussed efforts to curb excessive use of AI tokens within the company, according to interviews with multiple outlets. The executive addressed what some have termed tokenmaxxing, referring to overreliance on large language model queries.

Nadella emphasized the need for what he called full-stack builders and hyper-leveraged generalists in AI development. He also stated that everyone holds a stake in AI development, discussing Microsoft's approach to responsible deployment of the technology.

cards.headline: Hacking group claims breach of Oracle PeopleSoft servers at over 100 organizations
cards.teaser: Cybercriminals say they accessed Oracle PeopleSoft servers at more than 100 entities, including universities.
cards.body:
The ShinyHunters cybercriminal gang has claimed responsibility for compromising Oracle PeopleSoft servers across more than 100 organizations, with many of the affected institutions being universities.

PeopleSoft is an enterprise resource planning system that organizations rely on to manage critical functions including human resources, financial operations, and other business processes. The alleged breach represents a widespread security incident potentially affecting numerous institutions simultaneously.

cards.headline: Venus and Jupiter appeared close together in sky this week
cards.teaser: The two planets converged in a visible conjunction on June 9.
cards.body:
Venus and Jupiter appeared in close proximity in the evening sky on June 9 in an astronomical event called a conjunction. Multiple astronomy publications and outlets shared photographs of the planetary alignment.

The event, which some outlets described as a cosmic kiss, was visible to observers looking at the dusk sky. National Geographic and other publications provided guidance on viewing the phenomenon, which occurs when planets appear close together from Earth's perspective.

cards.headline: Ubisoft closes multiple studios, affecting up to 380 employees
cards.teaser: The video game company shut down offices in multiple cities as part of organizational restructuring.
cards.body:
Ubisoft announced the closure of multiple studios, with up to 380 employees potentially impacted by the restructuring. The affected locations include the company's Winnipeg studio, which employed approximately 65 people, and its San Francisco office.

The closures are part of broader organizational changes at the video game publisher. Ubisoft develops and publishes major gaming franchises and operates studios worldwide. The company framed the moves as part of restructuring efforts.

cards.headline: American Diabetes Association apologizes for removing scientists who criticized Trump
cards.teaser: The organization reversed course after initially defending its decision to eject researchers.
cards.body:
The American Diabetes Association apologized after ejecting scientists who had criticized former President Trump. The organization initially defended the decision before reversing course.

The incident highlighted how scientific organizations handle political speech. The ADA doubled down on its removal of the researchers for several days before ultimately issuing an apology.

hero.headline: Knicks complete largest comeback in NBA Finals history to take 3-1 series lead over Spurs
hero.body:
The New York Knicks mounted an extraordinary comeback from a 29-point deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4, securing a commanding 3-1 series lead and moving within one victory of their first NBA championship since 1973.

OG Anunoby delivered the decisive play with 1.2 seconds remaining, tipping in a missed three-pointer from Jalen Brunson to complete the historic rally in front of a stunned Madison Square Garden crowd. The 29-point deficit represents the largest comeback in NBA Finals history, surpassing the previous record of 24 points set by the Boston Celtics against the Los Angeles Lakers in 2008.

The Spurs dominated the early stages of the game, building a commanding lead behind their hot outside shooting. San Antonio hit 11 of their first 16 three-point attempts and led 41-22 after the opening quarter. By halftime, the Spurs had extended their advantage to 76-49, the largest halftime lead ever held by a visiting team in an NBA Finals game.

The Knicks' turnaround began in the third quarter when they held San Antonio to just 14 points on 4-for-20 shooting. The Spurs failed to score a single basket from the paint during that period, allowing New York to chip away at the deficit. A crucial fourth-quarter run sealed the comeback, with the Knicks outscoring San Antonio 28-9 over a seven-minute stretch.

Brunson broke through with a layup with 1:22 remaining to give New York its first lead of the game at 105-104. After the Spurs briefly retook the lead, Anunoby's tip-in secured the victory. Remarkably, the Knicks led for only 53.8 seconds of the entire game.

Anunoby finished with 33 points and made seven of nine three-pointers, both playoff career highs. Brunson added 36 points and seven assists, while Jose Alvarado contributed eight crucial points off the bench during the fourth-quarter rally.

For the Spurs, Victor Wembanyama recorded 24 points and 13 rebounds. Dylan Harper added 21 points while De'Aaron Fox and Devin Vassell each scored 18. San Antonio shot just 3-for-17 from three-point range after halftime and were outscored 58-30 in the second half.

The stunning victory took place in front of a star-studded Madison Square Garden crowd that included celebrities like Taylor Swift, Spike Lee, Ben Stiller, and Tracy Morgan.

With the series heading to San Antonio for Game 5, the Knicks can clinch their first championship in 53 years with a road victory. The Spurs must win to force the series back to New York. Only the 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers have previously overcome a 3-1 Finals deficit to win the championship.

cards.headline: Patrick Mahomes to become NFL's first $500 million player
cards.teaser: The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback is set to reach historic contract territory as the team prepares a new deal.
cards.body:
Patrick Mahomes has agreed to a restructured contract with the Kansas City Chiefs that pushes his total compensation past $500 million, making him the first NFL player to reach that milestone. The deal adds two years to his existing agreement, extending through the 2033 season when Mahomes will be 38 years old.

The contract is worth $504.75 million with incentives and escalators that could increase the value beyond $520 million. This follows Mahomes' 10-year, $450 million deal signed in 2020. Kansas City Chiefs chairman Clark Hunt described the quarterback as a "generational talent and elite human being."

cards.headline: Ja'Kobe Tharp breaks 110-meter hurdles world record at NCAA championships
cards.teaser: The American hurdler set a new global standard during preliminary heats at the college outdoor track championships.
cards.body:
Ja'Kobe Tharp set a new 110-meter hurdles world record during the heats at the NCAA Division I outdoor track and field championships on Wednesday. The collegiate athlete's record-breaking performance came during the preliminary rounds of competition.

The championships brought together top collegiate track and field athletes competing for national titles across multiple events and disciplines.

cards.headline: Germany players pay for 600 fans to travel to World Cup group stage finale
cards.teaser: The national team will cover bus transportation costs to New Jersey amid criticism of high travel expenses at the tournament.
cards.body:
Germany's national team players will pay for bus transportation for 600 supporters to attend their final World Cup group stage match in New Jersey. The players' decision responds to complaints about high transportation costs affecting fans' ability to travel during the tournament.

This gesture aims to help German supporters access the group stage finale, which will have significant implications for the team's advancement in the competition.

cards.headline: Wolves dismiss head coach Rob Edwards after seven months
cards.teaser: The Premier League club parted ways with their manager less than a year into his tenure.
cards.body:
Wolverhampton Wanderers have sacked head coach Rob Edwards after seven months in charge. Edwards, who took over last November following Vítor Pereira's departure, was unable to prevent the club's relegation from the Premier League. He inherited Wolves bottom of the league with just two points from 11 matches and could not improve their position sufficiently.

The club was relegated in April after eight years in the top flight. Edwards had signed a three-and-a-half year contract upon his appointment. Wolves are now targeting Portuguese manager César Peixoto as his replacement and have recently signed Kieran Trippier and Raúl Jiménez.

cards.headline: UFC Freedom 250 to take place at White House with President Trump attending
cards.teaser: Fighters arrive for the unprecedented event scheduled to be held on White House grounds.
cards.body:
The UFC will hold Freedom 250 at the White House with President Trump expected to attend the event. Fighters have arrived for what the organization is calling an innovative moment in UFC history, with participants expressing honor at competing in front of the president.

The event represents the first time the UFC has staged a card at the White House. The fight card and viewing details have been released as the promotion prepares for the historic venue.

cards.headline: Scotland midfielder Ryan Christie aims to make World Cup history
cards.teaser: The player cites painful memories from Euro 2024 as motivation heading into the tournament.
cards.body:
Scotland midfielder Ryan Christie is determined to make amends after Euro 2024, drawing on the disappointment of that campaign as fuel for the World Cup. He believes the squad carries a chip on their shoulder as they chase historic results.

This World Cup marks Scotland's first men's tournament appearance since 1998. The team hopes to progress further than in recent major competitions, with preparation focused on learning from past setbacks and strengthening team cohesion ahead of their group stage matches.

hero.headline: BigBang Announces 31-Show World Tour for 20th Anniversary
hero.body:
K-pop group BigBang will reunite for a 31-show stadium world tour celebrating the group's 20th anniversary. The tour marks the first time the group has embarked on a major trek since 2017.

The group, consisting of G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung, announced the tour on Thursday. The run will begin August 21 at Goyang Stadium in Goyang, South Korea, and continue through February 28, 2027. The extended schedule includes dates across multiple continents, reflecting the group's global reach and sustained popularity despite their extended hiatus from touring.

BigBang's previous world tour in 2017 came before the group entered a period of reduced activity, with members focusing on solo projects and completing mandatory military service. The reunion tour represents a significant return for one of K-pop's most influential acts, which helped establish the genre's international presence during their peak years.

The three-member configuration reflects the group's current active lineup. The announcement confirms the group's ability to fill stadium-sized venues across multiple markets, a testament to their enduring fan base. The tour's duration, spanning more than six months, indicates strong demand and logistical planning for what represents one of the larger K-pop touring commitments announced this year.

The August start date in South Korea follows the common practice of beginning international tours in the home market before expanding to other territories. The tour extends through early 2027, making it one of the longer anniversary celebration tours in recent K-pop history. Additional venue and city details were not provided in the initial announcement.

cards.headline: French Singer Patrick Bruel Under Formal Investigation for Rape
cards.teaser: French singer Patrick Bruel has been placed under formal investigation for rape after being released from custody under judicial supervision.
cards.body:
Patrick Bruel, a 67-year-old French singer and actor, has been placed under formal investigation for rape and sexual assault. The investigation covers four cases involving allegations of rape, attempted rape, sexual assault and sexual harassment. Bruel was released from custody and remains under judicial supervision as an examining magistrate reviews the evidence.

Bruel has denied all charges. More than 20 women have made allegations against him dating back to the 1990s, making this one of the most significant MeToo cases in the French music industry.

cards.headline: Emily Watson Named Jury President at Sarajevo Film Festival
cards.teaser: British actress Emily Watson will serve as president of the jury for the Feature Film Competition at the 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival.
cards.body:
Watson will lead the jury for the festival's Feature Film Competition Program. She will also receive the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at the festival in recognition of her contribution to world cinema.

Jovan Marjanovic, director of the festival, praised Watson as an actress whose work has made a significant impact. The 32nd edition of the Sarajevo Film Festival will honor Watson with both the jury presidency and the festival's honorary award.

cards.headline: Tony Leung Lines Up Three New Projects Including Johnnie To Film
cards.teaser: Actor Tony Leung Chiu-wai has three productions planned, including a Johnnie To film, an India-set project, and a serial killer streaming series.
cards.body:
The Hong Kong actor disclosed the upcoming projects while speaking ahead of his role as jury president at a film festival. The projects include a film directed by Johnnie To, a separate India-set production, and a streaming series spanning six or seven episodes.

In the streaming series, Leung will play a serial killer. The three projects represent a busy production schedule for the actor following his jury duties.

cards.headline: Jane Eyre Musical Sets U.K. Stage Debut With West End Stars
cards.teaser: The musical adaptation of Jane Eyre by John Caird and Paul Gordon will make its U.K. premiere at Southwark Playhouse Elephant in London.
cards.body:
Charlie Burn and Ashley Gilmour will lead the cast of the production when it opens August 28. The show will run through October 24 at the London venue, marking the first time the musical has been staged in the United Kingdom.

Burn recently starred as Cady Heron in Mean Girls on the West End. The Jane Eyre musical represents a new production for the venue, bringing the classic novel to the stage in musical form for British audiences.

cards.headline: Documentary Birds of War Secured for International Distribution
cards.teaser: The Sundance prizewinning documentary Birds of War has been sold to multiple territories and will receive an Oscar-qualifying theatrical run in the United States.
cards.body:
London-based Dogwoof closed international deals on the documentary following its Sundance prize. The company has secured distribution agreements across several territories and scheduled a U.K. premiere at Sheffield DocFest.

The film will receive a theatrical run in the United States that qualifies it for Academy Award consideration. Dogwoof launched the film's trailer ahead of its U.K. premiere, following the documentary's recognition at Sundance earlier this year.

cards.headline: Kenny Loggins and Kevin Bacon Perform Footloose on Classroom Instruments
cards.teaser: Kenny Loggins and Kevin Bacon joined Jimmy Fallon and the Roots for a performance using classroom instruments on The Tonight Show.
cards.body:
The musicians performed a medley of Loggins' greatest hits using instruments typically found in classrooms. The performance included the song Footloose, which famously appeared in the 1984 film starring Bacon.

The Tonight Show segment featured Fallon and the Roots, who are known for performing popular songs using unconventional instruments. The collaboration brought together the original singer and the star of the film that made the song a cultural touchstone.

hero.headline: Key US surveillance authority set to expire as Congress remains deadlocked
hero.body:
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act is on track to lapse Friday after Congress failed to reach agreement on renewing the spy tool. The authority allows US intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets outside the United States without a warrant and has been credited with providing more than half the content in the president's daily briefing.

Lawmakers in both parties have warned that allowing Section 702 to expire could threaten national security operations. Intelligence officials say the authority has helped prevent terror plots and other security threats. If the law lapses, intelligence agencies and telecommunications companies face legal uncertainty about ongoing surveillance activities.

The appointment of Bill Pulte as director of national intelligence has complicated renewal talks. Pulte lacks national security experience and has drawn criticism from lawmakers in both parties as a Trump loyalist. His selection has created new friction in negotiations that were already stalled over privacy concerns and oversight provisions.

The dispute over Section 702 reflects broader tensions over government surveillance powers and civil liberties protections. Privacy advocates have long pushed for reforms to prevent warrantless searches of Americans' communications that are incidentally collected under the program. Those reform efforts have clashed with intelligence officials who argue the tool is essential for tracking foreign threats.

Beyond the immediate Section 702 debate, civil liberties groups are raising concerns about how the government plans to use artificial intelligence for domestic surveillance. According to recent reporting, the Pentagon has sought to deploy AI tools to analyze bulk commercial data about Americans, including geolocation and web browsing information. Privacy advocates argue that AI could dramatically expand surveillance capabilities by automating the analysis of vast datasets at scale.

The concern centers on how federal agencies already purchase Americans' private data from commercial sources without court approval. Immigration enforcement agencies have used purchased cellphone location data and license plate information to target communities. The addition of AI tools could make this data collection and analysis faster, cheaper, and more comprehensive.

Civil liberties organizations warn that without new congressional safeguards, the combination of bulk data collection and AI analysis could lead to mass domestic surveillance. They point to historical examples of government surveillance abuses and argue that current laws have not kept pace with technological capabilities. The concern is that AI tools could enable the government to build detailed profiles of individuals' movements, associations, and political views with minimal human oversight.

Congress has until Friday to pass legislation extending Section 702 or face the first-ever lapse of the authority since its creation. The approaching deadline has not yet forced a breakthrough in negotiations between the White House and Capitol Hill. The broader questions about AI-powered surveillance and civil liberties protections remain unresolved.

cards.headline: Outgoing intelligence chief resisted early departure pushed by successor
cards.teaser: Tulsi Gabbard told Bill Pulte she needed White House confirmation before leaving her post early.
cards.body:
Bill Pulte called Tulsi Gabbard on Tuesday, informing her that Tuesday was her last day as director of national intelligence. Gabbard had previously announced plans to depart at month's end, not immediately. She insisted on hearing directly from the president or the White House before leaving early.

The exchange highlights ongoing tension following Trump's selection of Pulte to lead intelligence agencies. Lawmakers from both parties have questioned Pulte's lack of national security experience and his status as a Trump loyalist. Trump has instructed Pulte to execute an immediate downsizing of the intelligence director's office and pursue a short-term extension of expiring surveillance law, complicating bipartisan negotiations over renewing Fisa authorities.

cards.headline: Trump pushes third reconciliation bill with $350 billion for Defense Department
cards.teaser: The president called on Congress to immediately pass legislation that includes the Save America Act.
cards.body:
President Trump called on Republicans to immediately pass a third reconciliation bill worth $350 billion on Wednesday. The legislation would direct substantial funding to the Department of Defense and include the Save America Act, which Trump requested be added to the package.

The push represents Trump's effort to accelerate work on the spending measure, which is still being developed on Capitol Hill. The president framed the Defense Department funding as a key element of his legislative priorities as Republicans work to shape their next spending bill.

cards.headline: Trump remarks on inflation and midterms provide material for Democratic campaigns
cards.teaser: The president said he does not think about Americans' financial situation and does not care about the midterms.
cards.body:
President Trump made three statements over the course of a month that Democrats plan to use in campaign advertising ahead of the midterm elections. On May 12, Trump said he does not think about Americans' financial situation. Two weeks later on May 27, he said he does not care about the midterms. The president delivered a third quote that Democrats consider politically damaging.

The statements come as inflation remains elevated and Americans face rising prices. Democrats see the remarks as evidence that Trump is disconnected from voters' economic concerns. Republican strategists worry the quotes could prove difficult to defend in competitive races, giving Democrats ready-made attack lines for campaign advertisements.

cards.headline: House Democrat proposes restricting lawsuits over data center rejections
cards.teaser: Rep. Rob Bresnahan introduced legislation limiting companies' ability to sue municipalities that reject data center applications.
cards.body:
Rep. Rob Bresnahan of Pennsylvania introduced the Local Control Protection Act, which would restrict companies from suing municipalities that reject applications to build data centers. The bill would also require developers to file legally binding documents as part of the application process. The legislation responds to growing opposition to data centers in communities across the country.

Members of Congress are moving to capitalize on grassroots resistance to data center construction. Local communities have protested the facilities over concerns about noise, energy consumption, and environmental impact. Lawmakers see political opportunity in aligning with residents opposed to data center development in their neighborhoods.

cards.headline: World Cup preparations collide with immigration enforcement efforts
cards.teaser: Visa restrictions and immigration crackdowns have created tension ahead of the 2026 FIFA tournament on US soil.
cards.body:
President Trump has promoted the 2026 FIFA World Cup as an opportunity to showcase American leadership and unity on US soil. Stories of immigration crackdowns and visa restrictions in the run-up to the tournament have complicated that message. Visa barriers have affected people planning to attend the global sporting event.

The World Cup represents an early test of whether Trump can successfully host a major international event while pursuing his immigration agenda. The 2028 Olympics in the United States follow just two years after the soccer tournament. How the administration balances security priorities with facilitating international visitors will shape perceptions of both events.

cards.headline: House Democratic leader faces internal disagreement on economic priorities
cards.teaser: Hakeem Jeffries says Democrats will focus on affordability, but some members want other issues emphasized.
cards.body:
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has said his party will prioritize affordability as inflation continues to rise. Not all Democratic members agree with that emphasis. Some lawmakers argue the party's agenda should focus on other policy areas they consider fundamental to the Democratic platform.

The disagreement reflects different views within the Democratic caucus about how to respond to economic conditions and what message will resonate with voters. While Jeffries emphasizes pocketbook issues, other members want to keep attention on policies beyond economic relief. The internal debate will shape how Democrats present their agenda ahead of the midterm elections.
